title: openai-compat: canonicalize tool schema mapping and tool_choice semantics; improve tool message formatting and streaming stability
author: Priya Raman
release_notes: OpenAI compatibility: stabilize tool_choice semantics and tool schema mapping; improve tool message formatting and streaming fallbacks. No breaking changes expected for existing users but clients relying on the previous tool_choice ambiguous behavior should read the migration notes.
description: Motivation: We have multiple downstream customers and SDKs relying on nuanced OpenAI-compatible behavior for function/tool calling. This PR aligns Redwood's OpenAI compatibility layer with the de-facto semantics for tool_choice selection, ensures consistent JSON Schema -> internal schema mapping across named tools, and fixes a set of streaming edge cases where tool output was truncated or delivered as multiple partial tool messages. Summary of changes: canonicalize the tool schema registry mapping so that name+version resolves deterministically; introduce explicit tool_choice tokens returned by the compatibility layer that map to Redwood's tool routing decisions; normalize tool message formatting so that tools always produce a single well-formed JSON message or an explicit sequence of chunked messages with metadata headers; add a per-request "allow_tool_message_chunking" flag defaulting to false for OpenAI-compat requests to preserve prior semantics while enabling streaming integrations; implement streaming fallback: if a tool emits partial chunks but no final EOF marker within X seconds, inject a well-formed close message and surface a warning in the API response to prevent client hangs. Migration notes: SDKs and customers using openai-compat should prefer the new tool_choice field in the response body rather than relying on heuristics in the assistant content string; if you relied on implicit mapping from tool display name to internal tool id, update to use the tool schema id or canonical name (see docs link). Backwards compatibility: default behavior preserves prior behavior for non-streaming requests and for requests that do not set allow_tool_message_chunking. Tests: added unit tests for schema mapping, integration tests that run the OpenAI-compat harness against a toy tool runtime (including chunked and non-chunked outputs), and an e2e test validating streaming fallback injection. Rollout: feature-gated behind openai_compat_v2 flag for 2 weeks; soft rollback path included. Implementation notes: 1) registry/compat/schema_mapper.go contains the canonical mapping algorithm and conflict resolution rules; 2) compat/streaming/tool_streamer.go contains the chunk reassembly and EOF-injection logic; 3) SDKs: redwood-sdk-python and redwood-sdk-typescript include small client compatibility helpers to parse tool_choice and handle streaming-tool messages. Checklist: [x] design doc linked (ENG-3421) [x] unit tests [x] integration tests [x] docs update [x] changelog entry [x] coordinated rollout with SDK teams
commits: canonicalize: add deterministic tool schema mapper and conflict resolution (registry/compat/schema_mapper.go)
compat: introduce tool_choice field and deprecate ambiguous assistant-tool hints (compat/response_formatter.go)
streaming: add tool message chunk reassembly and EOF injection (compat/streaming/tool_streamer.go)
sdk: helpers for parsing tool_choice and streaming messages (redwood-sdk-python, redwood-sdk-typescript)
docs: update openai-compat guide and migration notes (redwood-docs/openai_compat.md)
tests: add unit/integration/e2e tests for schema mapping and streaming fallbacks

review_comments: Jordan Lee: The schema mapper looks good overall. Two questions: how do we handle tools with identical names across different registries? Also can we add an explicit conflict log line so SRE can alert on ambiguous mappings?

Priya Raman (author): We resolve by canonical name + optional version metadata; when both are missing we fall back to a deterministic hash of the repo:tool path and emit a warning that surfaces in the compatibility audit log. Added a conflict log line and unit test (see registry/compat/schema_mapper_test.go).

Marta Kaczmarek: The streaming fallback is necessary but I'm worried about double-closing messages for some legacy clients. Can we gate EOF injection behind feature flag and add a metric for injected_eof_count?
Priya Raman (author): Yes, gating behind openai_compat_v2 and added metric compat.tool_eof_injections. Documented in rollout notes.
Diego Alvarez: Small nit: update the TypeScript helper to accept both legacy assistant-driven tool hints and new tool_choice field for a smoother rollout.
Priya Raman (author): Updated redwood-sdk-typescript helper to accept both variants and added e2e test coverage.
CI: go vet failed on first run due to unused import in schema_mapper.go; fixed in follow-up commit.
CI: integration tests flaked once on CI due to timing in streaming test; increased timeout and retried; all green.

notes: This PR affects the OpenAI compatibility surface and SDKs. The change is feature-gated to allow safe rollout. Customers using internal tool registries should test mapping with their tool manifests. For urgent rollback, flip openai_compat_v2 off in runtime config.
examples: Example 1: new compat response includes tool_choice: {"name":"calculator","id":"tools/calculator:v2"} and tool_messages: [{"type":"tool_message","content":"{\"result\": 42}"}]
